lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Quick test. Count the people on a phone.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Don't lose count.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: How many?

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Five.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And the clown? You saw him, right?

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: In a real experiment, most people on a phone call never saw him.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Psychologist Ira Hyman needed a distraction nobody could miss. Then a student told him:

lines.speaker: STUDENT
lines.text: I own a unicycle.

lines.speaker: STUDENT
lines.text: ...and a clown suit.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So for one hour, the clown rode circles in the middle of campus.

lines.speaker: INTERVIEWER
lines.text: Did you see anything unusual?

lines.speaker: FRIEND
lines.text: The clown? He was amazing!

lines.speaker: HEADPHONES
lines.text: Dude, the unicycle guy!

lines.speaker: PHONE_GUY
lines.text: Sorry... what clown?

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Even asked straight out, only {1|one} in {4|four} people on a call had seen him.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Here's the weird part: people listening to music noticed him.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You see, a call pulls your mind toward someone who isn't there.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So Hyman tried something sneakier. He hung dollar bills on a branch, right at head height.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Nearly everyone ducked under it.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: On a phone? Only {6|six} in {100|a hundred} stopped for the money.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Their bodies dodged it. Their minds never saw it.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You counted five phones. You saw the clown.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Did you see the money?
